categories.name: Touches files it should not edit
categories.description: Hand-edits generated output, raw data dirs, symlinks/stubs, its own instruction file, or intentionally odd code.

categories.name: Unsafe or unrequested git / release actions
categories.description: Force-pushes, amends, skips hooks, runs git unprompted, wrong base branch, manual version bumps/publishing, wrong tags, leaves work unpushed.

categories.name: Commit/PR message and attribution form
categories.description: Adds or omits AI attribution, trailers, issue references; misstates own contribution.

categories.name: Scope creep and unrequested change
categories.description: Unrelated refactors, speculative features, proactive README rewrites, reverting others' changes, whitespace churn, creating stray files.

categories.name: False or weak verification
categories.description: Claims success without evidence, treats 'process started'/'tests pass' as done, regenerates goldens, weakens checks, skips suites, commits red.

categories.name: Epistemic shortcuts: guessing, relaying, flattering
categories.description: Guesses instead of admitting ignorance, repeats stale docs/defect records without checking, agrees automatically, misattributes results, hallucinated code.

categories.name: Wrong tool, command, or framework for this repo
categories.description: Reaches for the habitual default (npm, black, Pester, raw tool, nonexistent subcommand, banned action) instead of the project's one.

categories.name: Violates architecture / layering invariant
categories.description: Bypasses the sanctioned abstraction, puts logic or types in the wrong layer, breaks a project-specific design or parity contract.

categories.name: Breaks public contract or compatibility
categories.description: Changes URLs, API behaviour, settings defaults, packaging or runtime assumptions that external users rely on.

categories.name: Hides failures
categories.description: Swallows errors, skips silently, leaves success exit codes on failure, blanket lint suppression, band-aid fixes.

categories.name: Secrets, security and privacy lapses
categories.description: Commits or bakes credentials, exposes sensitive data, injection-prone shelling out, CSP violations, unsafe code, out-of-scope security testing, snooping the user's browser.

categories.name: Code style and naming habits
categories.description: Vague names, stutter, tabs, mechanical modifiers, class components, nested blocks, lint-rule violations, over-engineering (needless error handling, bolted-on code).

categories.name: Comment and docstring noise
categories.description: Comments that restate the code, separators, duplicated type info, wrong comment language, emojis, jargon.

categories.name: Documentation drift and duplication
categories.description: Changes behaviour without updating docs, updates only one copy, duplicates content across instruction/doc files, pollutes changelog.

categories.name: Wasteful or stuck operating behaviour
categories.description: Retries hung tools, scans whole repo, repeated tool calls, needless re-indexing, expensive API/compute spend, blocking on open questions.

categories.name: Bad tests
categories.description: Timing-based or live-account-dependent tests, missing tests for new behaviour, misplaced cleanup.

categories.name: Runtime agent conduct (non-coding)
categories.description: Rules for an agent acting as product persona: when to stay silent, not sharing findings between models, respecting leases, user's explicit wishes, DM style.

categories.name: Environment / concurrency traps
categories.description: Project-specific gotchas where a plausible action breaks something non-obviously: regenerating .env, parallelising unsafe state, stale closures, renderer misparse, wrong script copy.

notes: 161/200 coded guard=true. Decision rule used: guard=true when the text has a prohibition, an X-not-Y contrast aimed at what the agent should produce, a stop/ask, or a mandatory obligation whose omission is the guarded behaviour (s0005, s0037, s0049, s0128, s0148); guard=false for descriptions, status notes ('not yet implemented', 'there is no test suite'), troubleshooting fragments and permissions (s0038). Boundary cases: (1) descriptive facts containing 'not' that implicitly steer the agent - coded true when the avoided action is evident (s0010, s0020, s0025, s0043, s0067, s0149, s0185, s0196), false when purely architectural narration (s0017, s0075, s0096, s0138, s0186, s0193, s0180); these could reasonably flip. (2) 'no test suite / no linter' status notes (s0083, s0095, s0111, s0085) plausibly guard against inventing test commands but were kept false per the status-note instruction. (3) s0177 is a review checklist item (what to look for), coded true with origin because it recounts a past defect. (4) s0031 mentions 'never committed' for self-ignored scratch files; coded false as workflow description. (5) specific: rules naming a language/tool but pasteable into any repo of that stack (ruff not black, Bun not npm, functional React components, Go stutter) were coded generic; rules naming repo paths, own types or domain coded project. Non-guard units were all given specific='project' since they are repo descriptions. (6) origin was applied strictly: only s0065 ('learned the hard way'), s0069 (cost the owner time), s0126 (AI will hallucinate / repeated low-quality PRs), s0161 (bug was fixed, don't reintroduce), s0177 (past defect narrated), s0199 (Common Pitfalls). Several others describe a very precise failure signature (s0093, s0141, s0196, s0040) that looks experience-derived but does not say so - a latent-origin signal worth a separate code. Surprising: a sizeable share of rules are not about code at all but about honesty of reporting (false verification claims, relaying stale docs, misattribution) and about instruction-file self-maintenance (do not edit/duplicate/bloat the agent file). Some units address runtime persona agents (chat bot, game master, phone-call agent), not coding agents. Categories overlap: 'wrong tool' vs 'architecture invariant' and 'doc drift' vs 'touches files it should not' share members; n_estimates are approximate and sum above 161.
